title: Social Media Specialist
location: Remote — North, Central or South America
summary: Own strategy, content calendars, captions, community and growth for a roster of premium home building, design and lifestyle brands.
intro: Peak Exposure Media is a video-first content agency in Utah. We make cinematic, polished social content for premium brands in home building, design and lifestyle, and we act as the outsourced marketing department for most of our clients. We're hiring a full-time Social Media Specialist to own the accounts end to end: strategy, calendars, captions, scheduling, community management, monthly reporting and, above all, growth.

You'll work alongside our videographers and editors. They make the footage look incredible; you make sure it reaches the right people, says the right thing and turns into followers, leads and results the client can feel.
We hire for four things: creative bravery, excellence over easy, client obsession and an ownership mentality. If that sounds like how you already work, you'll like it here.
processNote: Our process has three steps, all before an interview. We reply to everyone within 24 hours of each step.

values.name: Excellence Over Easy
values.desc: Quality matters; don't rush or choose the easy route.

values.name: Client-Obsessed
values.desc: Care deeply about the client's results, not just completing deliverables.

values.name: Ownership Mentality
values.desc: Act like it's your company, not just a job.

assessment.title: Written Assessment
assessment.blurb: About 25 minutes. Six questions about how you think and write. Each answer is capped at 150 words.

questions.prompt: Look at this client account. In your first 30 days running it, what are the three changes you'd make to grow it, in priority order, and why those three?
questions.strong: Three specific, prioritized moves with reasons tied to the audience (affluent homeowners, architects, designers). Not "post more consistently" or "use trending audio." Red flag: generic advice that would apply to any account.

questions.prompt: Write two different hooks (the first line, under 10 words each) and one full caption for a Reel showing a luxury builder walking through a showroom they just finished for a high-end fabric brand. Audience: interior designers and architects.
questions.strong: Hooks are specific and create curiosity without clickbait; the two are different strategies, not rewordings. Caption sounds like a premium brand, has a point, and ends with a clear, low-friction CTA. Red flags: emoji walls, "Check out our latest project!", hashtag dumps.

questions.prompt: A client says: "We've been posting for three months and haven't gotten a single lead from Instagram." What do you do, step by step?
questions.strong: Separates what social can and can't do, asks about the funnel (profile, link, DMs, site, follow-up), looks at the data, then proposes a concrete change and a way to measure it. Owns it. Red flag: blames the client's product or lectures them about brand awareness.

questions.prompt: A Reel you were confident in got a third of the account's usual reach. Walk us through exactly how you'd diagnose it and what you'd change next.
questions.strong: Names actual metrics (3-second retention, average watch time, shares/saves vs. reach, follower vs. non-follower split) and reads them in order: hook, then content, then distribution. Ends with a testable change. Red flag: "the algorithm" or "post at a different time" with no evidence.

questions.prompt: You manage five accounts. It's 4pm, you're behind on tomorrow's posts for two of them, and a client emails asking for a "quick" new post about an award they won today. Tell us what you do over the next two hours.
questions.strong: Triage with a clear logic, communicates proactively with the client about timing, protects quality rather than shipping junk, and describes the system that stops this happening weekly. Red flag: either does everything at once or quietly drops something.

questions.prompt: On a client's post, a real past customer comments: "Beautiful photos. Shame they went 3 months over schedule on our house and never returned calls." Write your public reply word for word, then tell us what you'd do next behind the scenes.
questions.strong: The reply is calm, human, non-defensive, takes it offline and protects the brand without arguing in public. Behind the scenes: flags it to the client immediately, gets the facts, doesn't delete it unless there's a reason. Red flag: a template-y corporate reply, or deleting the comment.

test.title: Test Project
test.blurb: A real client, real assets, 4–6 hours of work over 72 hours. Unpaid, tightly scoped, and the single most important part of the process.
test.emailBlurb: The last step before a call is a scoped test project: a real client account, real assets, 4–6 hours of work.
packageNotes: The client's live Instagram: instagram.com/paragon_custom_construction — study it, that's your starting point
Raw footage and talking-head takes of Brandon Jensen (the owner) from a showroom build-out, in the folder above. Use it as source material for content ideas; you don't need to edit anything
No template, no reference plan, no brand guide. We want to see how you think, not a copy of ours

brief.p: Paragon Custom Construction — a high-end builder in Utah. They just completed a showroom build-out for Schumacher, a luxury fabric and wallcovering house. The account is well shot but under-strategized; it needs a point of view and a growth engine.
Affluent homeowners planning a custom build, plus the architects and interior designers who refer them. Visually literate, allergic to generic content, and they decide who to call based on trust.
Grow the account into a real lead source: more of the right followers, more saves and shares from the design community, and more inbound DMs and site visits from homeowners.
What's working, what isn't, and the three biggest growth levers. Be specific to this account; we'll know if it's a template.

Eight posts. For each: format (Reel, carousel, static, story series), the hook, the full caption, the CTA, and one line on why it's there. At least two posts must use the Schumacher showroom footage, and at least one must be built to earn saves or shares from designers.

brief.h: Deliverable 3 — One Reel concept, fully scripted
brief.p: Pick the best idea in your calendar that uses the showroom footage and write it out shot by shot for our editor: hook text on screen, the clips or takes of Brandon to use, the caption, and the cover text. You're not editing it; you're briefing it so well the editor doesn't need to ask a question.

Posting cadence by format, the growth tactics you'd run (and the ones you'd skip for this brand), the KPIs you'd report monthly with a target for each, and how you'd know by day 30 whether it's working.

Elegant and high-end with a working knowledge of what Instagram rewards. Think a luxury brand that understands social, not a social manager doing luxury. No emoji walls, no hashtag dumps, no "link in bio!" energy.
One Google Doc or Notion page we can open with the link, organized by deliverable. Polish matters, length doesn't. Set sharing to anyone with the link.
Your start and finish times — track them from the moment you open this brief to when you submit.

If you'd like, record a 2–3 minute Loom walking through your biggest strategic call and the post you're proudest of. It's optional, but it's the fastest way for us to understand how you think. Loom is free at loom.com — install the Chrome extension or desktop app, hit record with your screen and mic on, scroll through your doc while you talk, stop, and paste the share link below.
72 hours from when you unlock this page. Questions about the brief are welcome — there's a field for them below.

rules: The footage and the client are real. Nothing from this package may be posted, shared or used in your portfolio.
Don't contact the client or interact with their account during the test.
Questions are a good sign, not a weakness.
A late submission is still scored, but noted.

anchors.1: Generic advice that fits any account; growth plan is "post consistently"
anchors.3: Audit is specific to the account; levers are real; plan has targets
anchors.5: Sharp diagnosis, a clear point of view for the brand, and growth tactics chosen (and rejected) with reasons; you'd act on it tomorrow

anchors.1: Flat hooks, emoji walls, hashtag dumps, sounds like every builder account
anchors.3: Clean, on-voice captions with real hooks and a clear CTA
anchors.5: Hooks stop the scroll; every caption has a point; reads like a premium brand that gets social

anchors.1: Every post is the same format; Reel brief is vague or unusable
anchors.3: Formats matched to goals; Reel brief is clear enough to edit from
anchors.5: Uses the platform's mechanics on purpose (saves, shares, retention, collabs); Reel brief needs zero follow-up questions

anchors.1: No KPIs, or vanity metrics only; can't explain a dip
anchors.3: Right KPIs with targets; reads metrics in a sensible order
anchors.5: KPIs tied to the client's business, a day-30 kill/keep test, and diagnosis that reads like a growth lead's

anchors.1: Defensive, template-y or tone-deaf replies; would embarrass the client
anchors.3: Calm, human, takes it offline, protects the brand
anchors.5: Could be handed the client's inbox today; turns a complaint into trust

anchors.1: Missing a deliverable, ignored the audience or the feel
anchors.5: Hit every spec and made one smart call the brief didn't ask for

anchors.1: Doc is a mess; hours implausible; no system for juggling accounts
anchors.3: Clear doc, hours in the 4–6 range, a credible triage system
anchors.5: Doc a teammate could run from; efficient hours, better result; systems thinker

bravery.1: Plan and copy are safe and interchangeable; critique of the account is polite; can't name a risk
bravery.3: Makes one distinct strategic or creative choice and can defend it
bravery.5: The plan has a point of view; the audit is sharp and specific; rejects a popular tactic with a real reason

excellence.1: Shortcuts visible: template audit, thin captions, missed naming spec, no KPIs
excellence.3: Clean work, specs met, hours plausible
excellence.5: Every detail handled; doc reusable; chose the harder-but-better option and said so

client.1: Talks only about content; client is an obstacle; no mention of leads or business results
client.3: Frames the plan around the client's goal; handles pushback with questions, not defensiveness
client.5: Every choice is justified by what it does for the client's audience and pipeline; would calm an actual client

ownership.1: Blames client, algorithm or brief; no questions asked; late without notice
ownership.3: Owns the fix; hits the deadline; asks at least one clarifying question
ownership.5: Treats the account like their own business; flags a problem and solves it; explains trade-offs like a partner

decision.hireBar: Skill ≥ 4 and Values ≥ 4 after the call
